column1: # Bluetooth feature-generation map: which Core Specification version first
# introduced each feature, and how to recognise the specification text that
# spec_conf_requirements_generated.tsv extracts normative sentences from Core
# 6.3, which is a superset of every earlier generation.  This stack targets the
# Bluetooth 5.2 feature set plus Connection Subrating (a 5.3 addition), so a
# requirement governing a 5.4 or 6.x feature is not a gap in this stack; it is
# a feature the project never intended to build.  Counting it as uncovered
# inflates the gap and pollutes the ranked work list.
# Every "version" value below is taken from one of two machine-checkable places
# in Core_Specification_6_3.txt, and spec_conf_generation.awk re-reads both and
# fails if a row here disagrees with them:
#   [T42] Vol 0, Part D, Section 4, Table 4.2 "Features and their types",
#         which lists every feature added in version 1.2 and higher together
#         with the version that first introduced it.
#   [CH]  Vol 1, Part C, Sections 11.1-17.1 "New features", the per-version
# The "pattern" column is this file's only editorial content: it is the phrase
# by which the specification text for that feature is recognised.  Patterns are
# matched case-insensitively as substrings, never as regular expressions, so
# there is no hidden matching behaviour.
#   feature   feature name; must appear verbatim in [T42] or [CH]
#   version   Core version that introduced it
#   scope     in-scope-extra  counted as target even though version > 5.2,
#                             because the maintainer chose it AND the code
#                             implements it (evidence in the note column)
#   match     heading | text | both -- where the pattern may be matched.
#             "heading" patterns are matched against the section heading of the
#             requirement's own section and of its ancestor sections; "text"
#             patterns against the normative sentence itself.  A pattern is
#             restricted to "heading" whenever matching it against free text
# Two blocks: features introduced after the 5.2 target first (these are the
# rows that can change a requirement's scope), then features at or below it.
# Within each block, rows are ordered by feature name and then by pattern.
# Row order does not affect the result -- spec_conf_generation.awk always
# picks the most recent generation among all matching patterns -- but keeping
